# v1.1.0-dev.60 — Custom resolutions, and the zoom hotkey that actually fires

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.59`.

dev.59 added display scaling and resolution to profiles. This one
fixes the reason a lot of you would have pressed the hotkey and
seen nothing happen, and lets you type a resolution the driver
doesn't offer yet.

## The Hotkey Works Now

If you set up a profile with a scaling or resolution change in
dev.59 and its hotkey did nothing, this is why: the whole feature
sat behind a checkbox in Settings that shipped **off**, and when
it was off a load skipped the display block **without saying a
word**. Both halves of that were wrong.

The switch now defaults to on. It's still there as a kill switch
if you want it, but the reasoning for defaulting it off was
hollow — a profile can only have a display block if you built one
in the editor, so the switch was protecting nothing.

And if you do turn it off, a hotkey that hits a display block now
tells you so, in the status bar and a notification, naming the
setting that's blocking it. Saving a display block while the
switch is off simply turns it on, since saving one is a fairly
clear statement that you'd like it to apply.

## Custom Resolutions

Every resolution dropdown in the Display editor — the per-monitor
Resolution row and the zoom → resolution mapping — now ends in
**Custom…**, which opens width, height and refresh-rate boxes.

A custom mode your display doesn't currently offer is still
saved. It's shown as "not offered by this monitor yet" and
applies the moment the driver starts listing it. That matters for
virtual displays, where the mode list changes depending on what
the driver has been told about. If you had a resolution saved
that the current display can't do, it now shows up filled in and
marked unavailable, instead of the dropdown going blank.

## Registering Resolutions With Parsec

Parsec's virtual display only offers what its driver knows about.
There's a new **Parsec virtual display** section in the Display
editor that registers up to two custom resolutions directly with
that driver, behind one administrator prompt. Disconnect and
reconnect your Parsec session and they show up in Windows display
settings and in WLM's dropdowns.

Some plain talk about the limits, because the obvious expectation
here is wrong:

- **They will not appear in Parsec's own resolution picker.**
  That list is a fixed set built into Parsec, not read from your
  display. Apply the resolution from WLM instead, or set Parsec's
  host Resolution to "Keep Host Resolution" so it stops
  overriding what WLM sets.
- **Parsec owns three of the five slots.** Since Parsec 150-98 it
  rewrites slots 2, 3 and 4 on every connect with your client's
  screen sizes. WLM only ever touches slots 0 and 1, and shows
  you the other three read-only so it's clear what they are.
- Nothing refreshes the driver's list in place. It re-reads the
  registry when it creates a virtual display, which means a
  reconnect.

There's also a **Pull in unlisted customs** button that collects
every custom resolution you've already used in your mappings and
monitor settings that the display doesn't currently offer, so you
don't have to retype them.

## Smaller Things

- The monitor heading in the Display editor printed "primary"
  twice.
- Scaling and resolution dropdowns had no styling and rendered as
  bare white boxes.
- The mapping editor looked resolutions up under one key while
  the code that applies them checked several, so a Parsec display
  whose ID changed between sessions could show "No mappings yet"
  for mappings that were working fine.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
